name: Attacking 4-2-4

slots.why: Sweeper keeper covers the space behind a high line, which this shape leaves open.
Support full-back stays reasonably safe, because the wide attackers already supply the width.
Central defender marks the striker; with a high line there is little room for error, so pace matters. Cover is the alternate.
Cover centre-back sweeps up behind his partner, since runners in behind are the main danger against a line this high.
Support full-back on the right, holding a safer position while the wide attackers work the flank.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the second ball and starts the counter-press in the centre, where you are outnumbered.
Deep-lying playmaker is the only creative player in the middle and gets the ball to the four forwards quickly.
Inside forward cuts in from the left to attack the box alongside the strikers.
Winger stays wide and delivers, stretching the back line for the two strikers.
Deep-lying forward links the two wide players with the other striker, and is the one forward who drops to receive the ball.
Advanced Forward runs the channels to stretch the back line. Poacher is the alternate if he is more of a finisher than a runner.

description: A high-risk structure that immediately puts four players against the opposition back line and is intended to force the game.
whyGood: The DLF supplies some connection while the other three attackers threaten depth and width around the box.
whyThisShape: Four forwards and only two central midfielders: the most one-sided shape in the catalogue. Four attackers pin the opposition back line, and the two midfielders win the ball and feed it forward at once.
whenToUse: When chasing a game late, or against a much weaker side that will defend deep. It is a short-term tactic, not one for a whole season.
whenNotToUse: Against any side with quick forwards or good passing through the middle: two central midfielders cannot cover the space, and you will be opened up down the centre.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Stretches the opponent so the four forwards have space to work in.
instructionRationale.More Direct Passing: With only two midfielders, quicker forward passes skip the middle of the pitch entirely.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Gets the ball to the forwards before the defence has set.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Gives the fast forwards balls to run onto behind a high line.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Wins the ball back at once so you can attack again while the opponent is still out of shape.
instructionRationale.Counter: Attacks quickly on winning the ball, before the opposition can recover their shape.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Keeps the press high, so the attackers are supported by pressure on the ball.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Keeps the team compact so two midfielders have less ground to cover, at the cost of exposing slower defenders.

keyRequirements: Two midfielders able to cover huge spaces
